name: Shubham Dipak Gurav
project: Climate Resilient Agriculture Initiative, Integrating Agroforestry and Natural Farming
place: Peth, Bubnal, Mangle and Kuslewadi, Sangli district
deck: Four Natural Farming Schools in four Sangli villages. Jeevamrut, beejamrut, agniastra and neemastra made in the yard, in drums the farmers keep. A hundred and fifty people, six workshops, and a WhatsApp group that outlasted the project.
description: Four Natural Farming Schools across four Sangli villages: jeevamrut and neemastra made on the farm, in drums the farmers keep, for 150 people.

aims.h: Make the inputs on the farm
aims.p: Jeevamrut, beejamrut, agniastra, neemastra. Demonstrated, then handed over with the drums to prepare them in, because a recipe without a container is a lecture.
Training, field visits and peer learning across four villages, with a WhatsApp group so a question at six in the morning gets answered by somebody nearby.
A day on organic jaggery and the economics of natural sugarcane. A practice that costs a season of yield does not survive the season.
Mulching, cover crops and jeevamrut aimed at moisture retention first. Everything else on a rain-fed smallholding follows from whether the soil holds water.

did: Ran Natural Farming Schools in Peth, Bubnal, Mangle and Kuslewadi
Demonstrated jeevamrut, beejamrut, agniastra and neemastra, and distributed drums and containers to prepare them in
Held a one-day workshop on organic jaggery and the economics of natural sugarcane
Ran Soil School activities with village schoolchildren
Set up sticky traps for preventive pest management and demonstrated food forest and integrated farming plots
Kept a farmer WhatsApp group running for follow-up questions

quotes.text: Through this project, I learned how to prepare and use natural inputs like jeevamrut and neemastra. Earlier, I depended on chemical fertilizers and pesticides, but now I see improvement in soil moisture and reduced pest problems. This approach is low-cost and practical for small farmers like me.
quotes.speaker: Anil Kirpale

quotes.text: The Natural Farming School helped me understand how to use local resources for farming. I am now actively involved in preparing natural inputs and using mulching in my field. It has reduced my input costs and improved soil condition. I feel more confident to continue these practices.
quotes.speaker: Shrikar Gevari

quotes.text: Participating in this project and Soil School activities helped me understand the importance of soil and sustainable agriculture. This experience motivated me to stay connected with agriculture and environmental work.
quotes.speaker: Sagar Shelar

holes: One count of a hundred and more covers saplings planted and farmers trained together, so there is no way to say how many of each.
Rural is not ticked anywhere in the report. The urban, semi-urban and rural boxes are all blank; rural is read off the four villages the report names.
